title: A Healthy Heart
objective: After this level you can explain what keeps a heart healthy and what harms it.
summary: The heart muscle is fed by the coronary arteries; plaque narrowing them causes coronary heart disease and, if flow is suddenly blocked, a heart attack. The WHO and AHA name what affects heart health.

cards.headline: The heart feeds every part of you. So what feeds the heart?
cards.body: The heart muscle gets its own oxygen-rich blood through its own supply lines, the coronary arteries. When blood flow to part of the heart muscle is suddenly blocked, that's a heart attack. So what do public-health bodies say keeps those lines open?

cards.headline: Clogged supply lines
cards.body: In coronary heart disease, the most common type of heart disease, fatty deposits called plaque build up inside the coronary arteries and narrow them, so less oxygen-rich blood reaches the heart muscle. If blood flow to part of that muscle is suddenly blocked, it's a heart attack, and if flow isn't restored quickly, that part of the muscle begins to die. The pump that feeds everyone can run short of fuel itself.

cards.fact: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death worldwide.
cards.context: The WHO puts them at about a third of all deaths. It also says most cardiovascular disease can be prevented by addressing risk factors, and it names the most important behavioral ones for heart disease and stroke: unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, tobacco use and harmful use of alcohol.

cards.headline: The AHA's eight measures
cards.body: The American Heart Association sums up heart health in a list it calls Life's Essential 8. Four are behaviors: eating better, being more active, quitting tobacco and getting healthy sleep. Four are health factors to manage: weight, cholesterol, blood sugar and blood pressure (the same readings from Level 26). Sleep is the newest entry; the AHA added it in 2022.

cards.headline: A healthy heart: explained
learned: Coronary arteries feed the heart muscle itself
Plaque narrows them; a sudden blockage is a heart attack
WHO: leading cause of death, mostly preventable
AHA: Life's Essential 8 measures of heart health

questions.prompt: According to the NHLBI, what happens in a heart attack?

options.label: A heart valve closes permanently
options.rationale: Valves open and close with every beat.

options.label: The heart beats too slowly for a day
options.rationale: A heart attack is about blocked blood flow.

options.label: Blood flow to part of the heart muscle is suddenly blocked
The veins stop returning blood to the heart
options.rationale: The blockage is in blood flow to the heart muscle.

questions.explanation: A heart attack happens when blood flow bringing oxygen to part of the heart muscle is suddenly blocked.

questions.prompt: Which of these is on the WHO's list of the most important behavioral risk factors for heart disease?

options.label: Having type O blood
options.rationale: Blood type isn't on the WHO's list.

options.label: A resting pulse of 70
options.rationale: That's inside the normal resting range.

options.label: Healthy sleep
options.rationale: The AHA counts healthy sleep as good for heart health.

questions.explanation: The WHO names unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, tobacco use and harmful use of alcohol as the most important behavioral risk factors.

questions.prompt: Level 23 said arteries carry blood away from the heart. Which arteries carry oxygen-rich blood to the heart muscle itself?

options.label: The pulmonary arteries
options.rationale: They carry oxygen-poor blood to the lungs.

options.label: The venae cavae
options.rationale: Those are veins returning blood to the heart.

options.label: The capillaries of the lungs
options.rationale: They exchange gases, far from the heart muscle.

questions.explanation: The coronary arteries supply the heart muscle with oxygen-rich blood; plaque in them causes coronary heart disease.
